Through: Mr. Sumit  versus  STATE & ANR. 
 
 
 CORAM:
 HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE VIKAS MAHAJAN  
% 17.05.2023 CRL.M.A. 13321/2023(exemption)
1. Allowed, subject to all just exceptions.
2. Application stands disposed of.

3. The present petition has been filed under Section 482 CrPC seeking quashing of the FIR No.
472/2019 under Sections 498A/406/34 IPC registered at Police Station Tilak Nagar, Delhi, on the ground that the parties have entered into a settlement and the marriage between the parties has been dissolved by a decree of divorce by mutual consent.
4. Issue notice.
The learned APP for the State accepts notice.

5. The learned APP for the State submits that since the FIR has arisen out of a matrimonial dispute and there is a settlement between the parties, the State has no objection in case the FIR in question is quashed.

6. The petitioner no.1(former husband), petitioner no.2 (father of petitioner no.1), petitioner no.3 (mother of petitioner no.1), as well as, This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 24/09/2023 at 11:39:14 respondent no.2 are present in court and they have been identified by the Investigating Officer(I.O)
SI Purvi, P.S. Tilak Nagar.
7. The brief facts of the case are that the marriage between the parties was solemnised on 18.09.2012, as per the Hindu Rites and Ceremonies at Delhi.
Out of the said wedlock, two children namely Ms. Anaisha and Master Ayaan were born on 23.02.2015 and 23.10.2017.

sentences.text: On account of temperamental issues, certain disputes arose between the parties which led to various litigations between them, including the registration of the present FIR.
However with the intervention of respective parents, relatives and well-wishers, the petitioner no.1 as well as the respondent no.2 have settled their disputes.

9. In terms of the said settlement, the marriage between the petitioner no.1 and complaint no.2 has been dissolved by a decree of divorce by mutual consent under Section 13(B) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955.
10. It has been further agreed between the parties that the custody of both the children shall remain with the respondent no.2 and the petitioner no.1 shall not have any visitation rights.

11. It has been further mentioned in the petition that the terms of the settlement shall not be prejudicial to the interest of the children and the same shall not in any way affect their rights to claim maintenance etc., from the petitioner no.1 in accordance with law.

12. The respondent no.2, who is present in court states that she has given up all her claims as regards the maintenance, permanent alimony, stree dhan etc.
13.
On a query made by this court, the respondent no.2 states that she has entered into compromise out of her own free will and without any pressure, This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 24/09/2023 at 11:39:14 coercion or threat.
She further states that she has no objection, in case the FIR is quashed.

14. Having regard to the terms of the settlement which have been recorded in the present petition and the same being supported by the affidavits of the petitioners, as well as, by the respondent no.2 and considering the fact that the parties have mutually agreed to part their ways, no useful purpose will be served in continuing the proceedings, rather the same would create further acrimony between them.
15. It is, thus, in the interest of justice that the present FIR and all the other proceedings emanating therefrom be quashed.
16. In view of the above, there is no legal impediment in quashing the present FIR in question.
Accordingly, FIR No. 472/2019 under Sections 498A/406/34 IPC registered at Police Station Tilak Nagar is quashed along with all other consequential proceedings emanating there from.
17. The petition stands disposed off, in the above terms.
18. Order be uploaded on the website of this court.
VIKAS MAHAJAN, J MAY 17, 2023/
